questions.question: What is the largest animal on Earth?
questions.fact: A blue whale's heart is about the size of a small car, and its call can be heard hundreds of kilometres away underwater.

questions.question: What is a baby kangaroo called?
questions.fact: A newborn joey is only about the size of a jelly bean and climbs straight into its mother's pouch.

questions.question: How many arms does an octopus have?
questions.fact: Each of an octopus's eight arms has its own cluster of nerves and can "taste" what it touches.

questions.question: Which bird can fly backwards?
questions.fact: Hummingbirds beat their wings up to about 80 times a second, which makes the humming sound.

questions.question: What is a group of lions called?
questions.fact: Lionesses do most of the hunting for the pride, often working together as a team.

questions.question: Which reptile is famous for changing colour?
questions.fact: Chameleons often change colour to show their mood or control their temperature, not only to hide.

questions.question: Which bird is the fastest when diving?
questions.fact: A diving peregrine falcon can go faster than 300 km/h, making it the fastest animal on Earth.

questions.question: Which mammal can truly fly?
questions.fact: There are over 1,400 kinds of bats, about a fifth of all mammal species.

questions.question: What do giant pandas mainly eat?
questions.fact: A giant panda eats for up to 14 hours a day and can munch through about 12 to 38 kg of bamboo.

questions.question: Koalas mainly eat leaves from which tree?
questions.fact: Koalas sleep up to 20 hours a day, partly because eucalyptus leaves give them very little energy.

questions.question: What is a baby frog called?
questions.fact: Tadpoles breathe through gills like fish, then grow lungs and legs as they turn into frogs.

questions.question: Which is the largest species of big cat?
questions.fact: No two tigers have the same stripes, and their skin is striped too, not just their fur.

questions.question: Which egg-laying mammal has a duck-like bill?
questions.fact: When scientists first saw a platypus, some thought it was a fake made by sewing a duck's bill onto a beaver.

questions.question: Which animal is the symbol of the WWF?
questions.fact: The WWF chose the panda as its logo in 1961, partly because a black-and-white logo was cheap to print.

questions.question: How many humps does a dromedary camel have?
questions.fact: A camel's hump stores fat, not water. Camels can drink over 100 litres in a few minutes.

questions.question: What is a female deer called?
questions.fact: A male deer is a stag or buck, and only males of most deer species grow antlers, which fall off and regrow every year.

questions.question: What is the largest bird in the world?
questions.fact: Ostriches can't fly, but they can run at about 70 km/h, faster than any other bird.

questions.question: Which bird is famous for its colourful fan-shaped tail?
questions.fact: Only male peacocks have the famous tail. The females, called peahens, are brown.

questions.question: Why are flamingos pink?
options: Pigments in the food they eat
questions.fact: Flamingos are born grey. They turn pink from pigments in the algae and shrimp they eat.

questions.question: What is a group of wolves called?
questions.fact: Wolves howl to keep in touch with their pack, and a howl can be heard up to about 10 km away.

questions.question: What is a group of fish called?
questions.fact: Swimming in a school helps fish confuse predators and save energy.

questions.question: Which animal is called the "ship of the desert"?
questions.fact: Camels have three eyelids and two rows of long eyelashes to keep out sand.

questions.question: What do caterpillars turn into?
questions.fact: Inside its chrysalis, a caterpillar almost completely dissolves before rebuilding itself as a butterfly.

questions.question: Which reptile can live over 100 years and carries its home on its back?
questions.fact: Giant tortoises from the Galápagos and Seychelles can live well over 100 years. A tortoise called Jonathan is close to 200.

questions.question: What is the national animal of Scotland?
questions.fact: The unicorn became Scotland's national animal centuries ago, because it was a symbol of purity and strength.

questions.question: Which black-and-white striped animal lives in Africa?
questions.fact: Scientists think a zebra's stripes help keep biting flies away.

questions.question: What kind of animal is a Komodo dragon?
questions.fact: The Komodo dragon is the largest living lizard and lives on a few Indonesian islands.

questions.question: Which slow mammal spends most of its life hanging upside down in trees?
questions.fact: Sloths are so slow that algae grows on their fur, giving them a greenish camouflage.

questions.question: Which Mexican amphibian is famous for regrowing lost legs?
questions.fact: Axolotls can regrow legs, tail, and even parts of their heart and brain. In the wild they live only in lakes near Mexico City.

questions.question: How many legs does a crab have, including its claws?
questions.fact: Crabs walk sideways because of the way their legs bend.

questions.question: Which bird lays the largest eggs?
questions.fact: An ostrich egg weighs about 1.5 kg, about the same as two dozen chicken eggs.

questions.question: Which sea creature has no brain, heart or bones but can sting?
questions.fact: Jellyfish have existed for over 500 million years, long before the dinosaurs.

questions.question: What is the biggest fish in the world?
questions.fact: Whale sharks can grow to about 18 metres, but they eat only tiny plankton and are gentle with divers.

questions.question: What is a baby goat called?
questions.fact: Goats have rectangular pupils, which give them a very wide view to spot predators.

questions.question: Which animal is famous for building dams in rivers?
questions.fact: Beavers' teeth never stop growing and are orange because they contain iron.

questions.question: What colour is a polar bear's skin?
questions.fact: Polar bear fur isn't really white: each hair is clear and hollow, and only looks white as it scatters light.

questions.question: How do honeybees tell each other where flowers are?
questions.fact: The "waggle dance" tells other bees both the direction and the distance to the flowers.

questions.question: Which bird is a symbol of wisdom?
questions.fact: Owls can turn their heads about 270 degrees.

questions.question: What is a male duck called?
questions.fact: Only female ducks make the classic loud "quack"; male ducks make quieter sounds.

questions.question: Which insect's larva is farmed to make silk?
questions.fact: Silk was first made in China thousands of years ago, and the route it was traded along became the Silk Road.

questions.question: What kind of animal is an orca?
questions.fact: The orca, or killer whale, is the largest member of the dolphin family.

questions.question: What are animals that carry their babies in a pouch called?
questions.fact: Kangaroos, koalas and wombats are all marsupials. Most marsupials live in Australia and nearby islands.

questions.question: Which endangered eagle lives mainly in Spain?
questions.fact: The Spanish imperial eagle was close to extinction, but conservation work has helped its numbers recover.

questions.question: Which wild cat lives almost only in Spain and Portugal?
questions.fact: The Iberian lynx was the world's most endangered cat around 2002. Its numbers have grown into the thousands since then.

questions.question: Which fish is often called the fastest in the sea?
questions.fact: Sailfish can raise their big "sail" fin to herd fish into tight balls before attacking.

questions.question: Which animals live in an underground home called a "sett"?
questions.fact: Badger setts can be huge, with tunnels used by many generations over hundreds of years.

questions.question: Where do most penguins live in the wild?
questions.fact: Galápagos penguins live right on the Equator, and some islands they live on are just north of it.

questions.question: What is a baby swan called?
questions.fact: A family of swans is very loyal: many swan pairs stay together for life.

questions.question: What is a baby horse called?
questions.fact: Foals can stand and walk within hours of being born.

questions.question: What is the largest land carnivore?
questions.fact: Polar bears can smell a seal from more than a kilometre away.

questions.question: How many eyes do most spiders have?
questions.fact: Jumping spiders have excellent eyesight and can see colours, thanks to their large front eyes.

questions.question: Which bird is famous for copying human speech?
questions.fact: African grey parrots can learn hundreds of words, and some seem to understand their meaning.

questions.question: Which big birds often build nests on church towers in Spain?
questions.fact: White storks spend winter in Africa, but many now stay in Spain all year thanks to food in rubbish dumps.

questions.question: What is the largest primate?
questions.fact: Gorillas share about 98% of their DNA with humans and live in family groups led by a silverback.

questions.question: A mule is a cross between a male donkey and a female…
questions.fact: Mules are usually unable to have babies of their own.

questions.question: Which mammal can live for about 200 years?
questions.fact: Bowhead whales live in Arctic waters and can break through ice with their huge heads.

questions.question: What do we call an animal that eats both plants and meat?
questions.fact: Bears, pigs and humans are all omnivores.

questions.question: Dolphins breathe through a…
questions.fact: Dolphins sleep with only half of their brain at a time, so they can keep breathing and watch for danger.

questions.question: Which African animal is famous for its laugh-like call?
questions.fact: Spotted hyenas also hunt for most of their food; they don't only scavenge.

questions.question: Which tiny insect can carry many times its own body weight?
questions.fact: Leafcutter ants farm their own fungus, feeding it with the leaves they carry.

questions.question: What is a group of crows called?
questions.fact: Crows can recognise human faces and remember people who treated them badly.
